solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bustling bar seen in Indian city

indicators.note: bustling suggests busy jostling movement, so the letters of the next words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A busy bar is spotted somewhere in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bustling' looks like a description of the bar, but it tells you to rearrange BAR SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Benares is the older name of Varanasi, the holy city on the Ganges in northern India.

clue.text: Book omitting nothing restricted by embargo from servants in service

indicators.note: restricted by says the trimmed book sits confined inside the word for embargo

parts.note: an embargo is a ban

indicators.note: omitting says the letter for nothing is dropped from the book

parts.note: a tome is a book, especially a large one
O, zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Servants are barred from a book by a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in service' here means the armed services: a batman was an officer's personal servant in the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Batmen were soldiers assigned as personal attendants to officers, so military servants.

clue.text: No illegal trader is still expecting deliveries

parts.note: taken as written
a tout sells tickets unofficially at inflated prices

explanation.surface: A trader with no shady dealings is waiting for parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' are balls bowled in cricket: a batsman NOT OUT is still in and still facing them.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman who is not out remains at the crease, still facing bowlers.

clue.text: Money received? Hand a note found amongst half of receipts

indicators.note: found amongst says the hand, a and note sit inside the half-word
half of takes the first half of the letters of receipts

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Cash comes in, with a hand and a note discovered among half the receipts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that money sent is money received at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: A remittance is a sum of money sent to someone, which they receive as payment.

clue.text: Senior, retaining support, giving direction

indicators.note: retaining says the abbreviation holds the support word inside it

parts.note: a tee is a peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: An elder keeps backing someone while giving them guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a piece of guidance or advice pointing someone the right way.

clue.text: Take up residence around a US city

indicators.note: around says the phrase for taking up residence goes round the single letter that follows

parts.note: to take up residence somewhere is to settle there

explanation.surface: Someone moves in near an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State, in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Rugby in a whirl after team has redeployed dubious player

indicators.note: after says the rugby abbreviation comes behind the rearranged letters
redeployed means rearranged into new positions, so the letters are reordered
in a whirl says the abbreviation spins round and is read backwards

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A rugby side, reshuffled, fields a suspect player.
explanation.walkthrough: A shamateur is a sportsman officially amateur but secretly paid, a charge often made in old Rugby Union.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamateur poses as unpaid while taking money, so is a sportsman of doubtful status.

clue.text: Keen writer of religious songs missing No 1 slot

indicators.note: missing the number one slot means losing the first letter

parts.note: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic hymn-writer fails to reach the top spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic, as a keen fan is.

clue.text: Kitchen item mostly drawn in bluish-green

indicators.note: in says the trimmed word sits inside the colour word

parts.note: teal is a dark bluish-green colour

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: drawn, as of a vehicle pulled along, means towed

explanation.surface: A kitchen object is mostly sketched in a teal shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' suggests sketching but means pulled, TOWED, cut to TOWE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea towel is a cloth used in the kitchen for drying dishes.

clue.text: Something taking no end of time

definitions.text: Something taking no end of time

parts.words: Something taking no end of time
parts.note: something that takes endless time, an infinite span; 'no end of time' reads both as a lot of time and as time without an end

explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' usually means a great deal; here it is literal: time with no end.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is infinite or unending time, a span that never finishes.

clue.text: Betting system followed by millions is a symbolic thing

indicators.note: followed by says the betting system comes first, with the next piece placed after it

parts.note: the tote is the totalisator, a pool betting system used at racecourses
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A gambling scheme backed by huge sums becomes an emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem treated as a symbol of a clan or group.

clue.text: I created a grisly murder

indicators.note: grisly, gruesome and mangled, tells you the words before it are torn apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession: the speaker devised a gruesome killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murder' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb definition; 'grisly' rearranges I CREATED A.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or destroy completely, as a killer does a victim.

clue.text: A hill I observed occupying level around central area

indicators.note: occupying says the hill-and-letters group sits inside the word for level

parts.note: level, as in even or on a par, means equal
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone notes a hill set on flat ground near the middle of a region.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own A ends up after the hill and the I, so the pieces do not follow the clue's order; 'observed' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Equatorial describes what lies near the equator, the central band circling the globe.

clue.text: Nothing evident in staff complaint

indicators.note: in says the zero-letter goes inside the word for staffing

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: No grievance is apparent among the employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like a noun (employees) but is the verb to man.
explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a grumble, an expression of dissatisfaction.

clue.text: Rental arrangements have a reduced impact in outskirts of Leeds

indicators.note: in says the phrase for lessening goes inside the outer letters
outskirts of takes the first and last letters of Leeds

parts.note: to ease back is to lessen effort or intensity

explanation.surface: Property lets in the suburbs of Leeds are making less of a splash.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaseback is a deal where a seller leases back the property just sold, so a rental agreement.

clue.text: Decaying material requiring moderate line in dispersal

indicators.note: in dispersal means scattered about, so the letters of the two words are spread and reassembled

explanation.surface: Something rotting calls for a measured approach when it is broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioelement is a radioactive element, one whose nuclei decay, giving off radiation.

clue.text: Surrounded by rising worry, European about to meddle

parts.note: to be surrounded by something is to be in it

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to fret is to worry
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Hemmed in by growing anxiety, a European is about to interfere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of'; 'about' is RE and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere is to meddle, involving oneself where one is not wanted.

clue.text: Film plan has trail stopping short above a city

indicators.note: above, in a down clue, says the trimmed trail sits on top of the rest
stopping short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a scent is a trail left for hounds to follow
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A film outline has a trail that halts over a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline or script of a film's plot.

clue.text: First of German airmen's velocity mostly doing for scuttled battleship

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, are airmen; the 's adds no letter

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: velocity is speed

explanation.surface: German aircrew's speed helps sink a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Admiral Graf Spee was a German warship scuttled by its crew off Montevideo in 1939.
explanation.definitionFit: The Graf Spee was a German pocket battleship deliberately sunk by its own crew in 1939.

clue.text: Source of funny picture: nude figure heading off behind vehicle, one beside college

indicators.note: beside says the numeral for one sits next to the letter for college
behind says the trimmed nudist comes after the vehicle and the other pieces

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a naturist is someone who goes unclothed, a nudist

explanation.surface: A joke drawing shows a naked man losing his head behind a car near a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricaturist draws exaggerated, comic portraits, so is the producer of humorous pictures.

clue.text: Town's target: to block most of local feature getting upset

indicators.note: to block, to stop a passage, says the target word is lodged within the other piece
getting upset, in a down clue, says the piece is turned over and read upwards
most of says the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a lake is a feature of the local area
an end is an aim or target

explanation.surface: A town's aim is to obstruct a local landmark that is being toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town's' stands for 'Town is'. The lake is local because the town sits by the Lake District; it is a market town in Cumbria, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendal is a market town in Cumbria, in north-west England, on the edge of the Lake District.

clue.text: Stick poster nowhere else

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, such as a poster
being here and nowhere else means just here

explanation.surface: An instruction to fix a placard only in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick poster' reads like a bill-sticking order, but 'Stick' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface.

clue.text: Scent somewhat ambrosian if fierce

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A perfume that is partly heavenly and partly overpowering.
explanation.walkthrough: NIFF is British slang for a smell, usually an unpleasant one.
explanation.definitionFit: Niff is informal British slang for an odour, typically a bad one, so a smell or scent.

clue.text: Mule, say, angry about standing in bottom of river

parts.note: to be cross is to be angry

indicators.note: standing in says the word for about is placed inside the riverbed

parts.note: the bottom of a river is its bed
RE is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A furious mule stands in a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is a hybrid of a horse and a donkey, an example of a cross-bred animal.

clue.text: Expert player clutching one stringed instrument

indicators.note: clutching says the star word holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: a star is a top performer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A virtuoso grips a single stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked lute of Indian classical music.

clue.text: Times Square's filled with rubbish

indicators.note: Times Square is said to be filled with the answer, so it sits inside those words

explanation.surface: The New York square is strewn with litter.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Times' into 'Square'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is untidy clutter or rubbish lying about.

clue.text: Salesman to begrudge exhibit

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to begrudge something is to resent it

explanation.surface: A sales agent is jealous of a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibit' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent can mean to show or portray, as a painting exhibits or depicts something.

clue.text: Act as beggar, getting day in prison

indicators.note: in says the letter for day is placed inside the word for prison

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, so a prison

explanation.surface: A vagrant pleads, earning a day behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to scrounge or ask for things free, as a beggar does.

clue.text: Take charge of poetry in Old English

indicators.note: in says the poetry word is set inside the abbreviation for Old English

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone is put in charge of Anglo-Saxon poems.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or be in charge of something.

clue.text: Determination to start this again?

definitions.meaning: to solve this puzzle once more from scratch

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: 'this' is the crossword itself, which you would solve again.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve as a noun is firm determination; split as re-solve it means to work out a puzzle anew.
